You are a professional biblical lexicographer fluent in Spanish. Translate the following English lexicon entry into Spanish.

Lemma: G1096

ENGLISH GLOSSES TO TRANSLATE:
  Terse gloss: "To become, happen, come into being, or exist; spanning transformation, event occurrence, arrival, birth, and states of being"
  Readable gloss: "One of the most versatile verbs in the Greek New Testament, ginomai covers a vast semantic territory from becoming and happening to being born and simply existing. In narrative it signals pivotal transitions ('and it came to pass'), while in prayer it voices the deepest petitions ('let it be done'). Paul commandeers its optative form me genoito as his signature exclamation of horrified rejection. Across Arabic, Korean, and Swahili, translators must reach for entirely different roots depending on the sense, revealing just how much semantic work this single Greek verb performs."

SENSES:
  Sense 1: "become, change state"
    Enriched: The primary transformative sense: to undergo a change of state, to become something one was not before. Arabic sara and Korean doeda both denote change-of-state transitions. This covers the majority of occurrences (421x) including formulaic 'and it came to pass' narrative pivots (Matt 1:22; Matt 7:28) and statements of transformation like 'the Word became flesh.'
    Existing Spanish translations: fue, ha-habido, ha-sucedido, hubo, llegó-a-ser, quedó, sucedió
  Sense 2: "happen, occur, take place"
    Enriched: Denotes an event taking place or occurring, without implying personal transformation. Arabic hadatha 'it happened' and Korean ireonada 'to arise/occur' mark this as event-occurrence rather than state-change. Frequently introduces temporal clauses in the Gospels (Matt 8:16; Matt 14:15) and Acts narrative transitions.
    Existing Spanish translations: Aconteció, Llegó-a-haber, Sucedieron, Sucedió, Surgió, sucedió
  Sense 3: "come, arrive, appear"
    Enriched: Physical or temporal arrival into a place or situation. Where sense 1 transforms and sense 2 reports events, this sense moves a person or thing into view. Arabic ja'a 'to come' and Swahili -kuja confirm spatial movement. Mark uses this for John appearing in the wilderness (Mark 1:4) and evening coming (Mark 1:32).
    Existing Spanish translations: Estuvo, aconteció, llegando, llegó, venir, vino
  Sense 4: "let it be, may it be done"
    Enriched: Jussive or imperatival wish: 'let it be done,' 'may it happen.' Arabic li-yakun and Korean doera express the volitional dimension. Central to the Lord's Prayer (Matt 6:10 'your will be done') and Jesus's healing declarations (Matt 8:13; Matt 15:28), this sense carries the weight of divine petition and authoritative command.
    Existing Spanish translations: Hágase, Sea-hecha, esté, háganse, hágase, llegue-a-ser, sea, sea-hecha, sea-hecho, suceda
  Sense 5: "may it never be!"
    Enriched: Paul's emphatic negative optative me genoito: 'May it never be!' — a formula of absolute rejection appearing 16 times, mostly in Romans and Galatians. Arabic hasha and Korean geureol su eopda convey the same horrified dismissal. This idiomatic usage (Rom 3:4, 6, 31; Gal 2:17) functions almost as an interjection, rhetorically shutting down false conclusions.
    Existing Spanish translations: haya, sea, sea!
  Sense 6: "be, exist, find oneself"
    Enriched: Simple existence or static being without transformation: to be present, to find oneself in a state or location. Arabic kana 'to be' and Korean itda 'to exist' distinguish this from dynamic becoming. Appears in locative contexts like 'being in Bethany' (Matt 26:6) and statements of simple presence (Mark 9:33).
    Existing Spanish translations: estando, estar, estuve, fuiste, habiendo-estado, llegué-a-estar, se-hace, se-hagan
  Sense 7: "be made, be done"
    Enriched: Passive resultative sense: to be made, manufactured, or brought about by an external agent. Arabic suni'a 'it was made' and Korean mandeurejida confirm passive creation. Seen in 'the Sabbath was made for man' (Mark 2:27) and references to miraculous works being done (Acts 19:26).
    Existing Spanish translations: fue-hecho, hecha, hechos, llegando, se-ha-hecho, surgiendo
  Sense 8: "be born, come into existence"
    Enriched: To be born, to come into existence through origination. Arabic mawludan 'born' and Korean nada 'to be born' specifically mark natal beginning. Central to Christological statements: John 1:6 ('there was a man sent from God'), John 8:58 ('before Abraham was, I am'), and Paul's 'born of a woman' (Gal 4:4).
    Existing Spanish translations: Llegó-a-ser, fuera, llegado-a-ser, nacido
